test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A bus travelling at 99 km/hr completes a journey in 20 hours. What should its speed be to cover the same distance in 12 hours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is **constant**, **speed** is **inversely proportional** to **time**.

**Time ratio** = 20 : 12 = 5 : 3

**Speed ratio** = 3 : 5

Given: 3 units → 99 km/hr (since 1 unit = 33)

New speed: 5 units → 5 × 33 = 165 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 165 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial speed = 99 km/hr, Initial time = 20 hours, New time = 12 hours.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2eb6f4277a20ce1dee096d9a14fd19b1ffb3d95c6521e4cb1efc4e1d83b8442b.png] 

⇒ Total Distance = 99 km/hr × 20 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 1980 km

⇒ New Speed = Total Distance ÷ New Time

⇒ New Speed = 1980 km ÷ 12 hours

⇒ New Speed = 165 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 165 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation Property

If Distance is constant, S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂. This allows for quick calculation of speed or time when the other variable changes.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

For the same distance traveled at two different speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p
